function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Java is a high‑level, class-based, object‑oriented programming language designed to have as few implementation dependencies as possible. It was originally developed by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle Corporation) and released in 1995. Key features include:

1. **Platform Independence** – Write once, run anywhere (WORA): Java programs compile into bytecode which runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), allowing them to execute on any device equipped with a JVM regardless of underlying hardware or operating system.

2. **Object-Oriented Design** – Everything revolves around objects and classes, promoting modularity, reusability, and maintainable code through encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.

3. **Robust Standard Library** – The Java Development Kit (JDK) provides extensive APIs covering networking, I/O, concurrency, collections, GUI development (Swing/AWT), database connectivity ( JDBC ), XML parsing, cryptography, and more.

4. **Strongly Typed & Safe** – Compile-time checks catch many errors early, while runtime safety mechanisms such as automatic garbage collection reduce memory leaks and pointer-related bugs common in languages like C/C++.

5. **Multithreading Support** – Built-in support for concurrent execution via threads, synchronization primitives, and higher-level utilities in `java.util.concurrent`.

6. **Enterprise Use** – Widely adopted for building web applications (Servlet/JSP, Spring framework), enterprise services (EJB, JPA), Android mobile apps, big-data processing frameworks (Hadoop, Spark), IoT devices, and embedded systems.

7. **Community & Ecosystem** – Rich ecosystem of open-source libraries, IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, NetBeans), build tools (Maven, Gradle), testing frameworks (JUnit, TestNG), and continuous integration pipelines.

In short, Java remains one of the most popular, versatile, and widely supported programming languages across industries due to its portability, performance, security, and mature tooling.
